description: State of Alaska Open Data Geoportal is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by State of Alaska. This tool provides access to location-based data, maps, and applications, which makes the state's vast collection of spatial data easier for the public to locate and use. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Air Quality, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal, Landslides, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Water Quality. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Cultural and Community Services, Energy and Utilities, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Transportation and Mobility, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
